admission.justification: The shared hover/focus/membership contract spans one common control and independent task/review/nested-object hosts. Keeping the host rules and mounted surfaces coherent prevents quietness or nested isolation from depending on unrelated reference-identity or send-transaction promises.

applicability: Shared AddToTray reference-object controls mounted inside addToTrayHost on the intent-review invariant/family/block/entry, Code without invariant file/hunk, comparison change-set and canonical task-document surfaces inspected at A4-F5.
conditions: An idle control is quiet while its own host is neither hovered nor focused; hover or focus-within of that host reveals it. A nested idle host still hides its own control when only its outer host is active.
The native button is named for its object. Keyboard focus exposes its focus style; an already collected object remains named, displays ✓ in tray and ignores further collection clicks.

A first collection delegates at most one reference to the store under current admission bounds. Store membership uses the exact object key; refusal leaves the offer uncollected rather than promising a successful add.
A task header supplies one offer only with its canonical document reference; review subjects/blocks/change sets supply offers only when their required comparison/pick identity exists.
exclusions: Standalone AddToTray controls outside addToTrayHost intentionally remain visible; this quiet-host policy does not require an invisible standalone control.
The File Viewer line gutter is its own pointer/keyboard control and is not this shared AddToTray component.
Reserved lane rows use hidden replicas for sizing, not active collection offers; the Knowledge page and ordinary Operations task rows receive no new object offers.
This does not change exact reference snapshot identity, copy/selection preservation, recipient choice, message filing or send settlement.
CSS-selector fixture inspection is not a fresh real-browser cascade or host visual acceptance.
